To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Hypocoercivity of Fokker-- Planck equations with linearly growing drifts is equivalent to confinement and hypoellipticity; (2) The existence of a unique steady state for the linear drift Fokker--Plank equation is equivalent to confinement; (3) Hypocoercive FPE with linear drift have an exponential convergence rate of order $1$; and (4) The convergence rate of the linear drift FPE is independent of the growth rate

(1) the existence of a normalised steady state is equivalent to the fact that the system is hypoelliptic, and (2) if the system is hypo-elliptic, the solution to the Fokker--Plank equation converges exponentially towards equilibrium.

(i) The steady states of the system are given explicitly by the product of the steady state of the drift term with the steady state of an auxiliary diffusion operator, which can be computed explicitly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of hypocoercivity for linear Fokker-- Planck equations with linear and possibly non-symmetric drifts.
the existence, uniqueness and exponential decay of solutions for a class of Fokker-- Planck equations on the real line.
the study of the large time behaviour of solutions to the linear Fokker--Plank equation on the whole space, with a drift term that is linear in the position and possibly non-symmetric.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is hypoelliptic, confined and hypocoercive if and only if it has a unique normalised stationary state.
for the class of Fokker--Plank equations considered in this thesis, existence of a steady state is equivalent to the system being hypocoercive.
, if the system is hypocoercive, then the steady state is unique, and if the steady state is not unique, the system is not hypocoercive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish the exponential decay of solutions to the Fokker-Plank equation in the case of linear drift and non-symmetric collision operators.
we establish that for the linear drift Fokker--Plank equations on the whole-space, hypoellipticity and confinement of the drift are sufficient conditions to guarantee exponential decay.
the existence of a normalised steady state and the exponential convergence to it for the hypocoercive equations with linear drift are equivalent.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the class of linear drifts, the steady state can be computed by solving a system of ordinary differential equations and the exponential convergence can be obtained by solving a Lyapunov equation
the non-symmetry of the Fokker--Plank operator does not affect the exponential decay of the solution.
the non-symmetry of the generator of the Fokker--Plank equation does not prevent exponential convergence to equilibrium.
